gloss: botamochi; rice cake coated with sweet red bean paste

definitions.gloss: botamochi; sticky rice ball coated with sweet red bean paste
definitions.explanation: A traditional sweet made of pounded glutinous rice formed into a ball and covered with あんこ (sweet red bean paste). It is closely associated with the spring equinox, when it is offered to ancestors.

examples.japanese: {牡丹餅|ぼたもち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
⟦お{彼岸|ひがん}→お彼岸：08933_ohigan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{牡丹餅|ぼたもち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{供|そな}える→供える：11562_sonaeru⟧。
examples.english: We offer botamochi at the equinox.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{彼岸|ひがん}→彼岸：12612_higan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧{牡丹餅|ぼたもち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}って→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother always makes botamochi for the spring equinox.

notes:
Named after the ⟦{牡丹|ぼたん}→牡丹：13488_botan⟧ (peony), a spring flower. The same sweet eaten at the autumn equinox is usually called ⟦おはぎ→おはぎ：29365_ohagi⟧, named after the bush clover ({萩|はぎ}) that blooms then.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- Strongly tied to ⟦お{彼岸|ひがん}→お彼岸：08933_ohigan⟧ (the equinoxes), when it is offered at family altars and graves
- Source of the proverb ⟦{棚|たな}→棚：01650_tana⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{牡丹餅|ぼたもち} ("botamochi from a shelf"), meaning an unexpected stroke of luck
